summary: Cancel-then-retry race: long-running function-call confirmation mismatch causing duplicate executions
description:
Issue summary:

Customer reports that when a client cancels a long-running function call (tool invocation) then immediately retries the same logical operation, the downstream function can execute twice and produce duplicate side effects. This appears to be most common with long-running handlers (>30s) where the server acknowledges the funcall start, the client cancels (AbortController / context cancel) and retries; the first run completes later and the customer observes duplicate side effects (e.g., duplicate emails, duplicate database writes).

Impact:
- Observable duplicate side effects for critical actions (billing emails) for a small subset of requests (~0.2% of calls from the customer).
- Customer on Dedicated capacity; duplicates break idempotency expectations and require manual reconciliation.

Environment:
- Customer: NimbusAI (dedicated cluster)
- Region: us-east
- SDKs observed: Go v0.9.3, Python v1.4.1
- Server runtime: dedicated-serving v2026.02.14

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a function call that triggers a downstream action taking 40–90s (handler sleeps then writes to external DB).
2) After 2–4s, client cancels request using context.Cancel (Go) or AbortController.abort (TS) or requests.Session.close (Python) and immediately issues a retry of the same logical operation (new request, same business id).
3) Observe: new request completes successfully; later the original inflight request completes on server side and triggers the same downstream action again.

Expected behavior:
- Either the initial inflight execution should be safely deduplicated on completion (server-side dedupe keyed by idempotency/business id) or the retry should be rejected/queued until the server can confirm the original outcome. Customer expects at-most-once semantics for business operations when they provide a request-level idempotency key.

Logs / Traces (sanitized excerpts):
- Client (Go): context cancelled -> reconnect -> new request 202 Accepted -> result returned to client after 3s
- Server trace: funcall-start id=call-abc123 timestamp=10:01:12 -> func invoked on worker-17 -> no explicit commit recorded yet
- Server later: funcall-complete id=call-abc123 timestamp=10:01:58 -> downstream webhook POSTed
- New request trace: funcall-start id=call-def456 timestamp=10:01:15 -> func invoked -> func completed timestamp=10:01:18 -> webhook POSTed

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis A: client-side cancel only severs the connection but does not communicate intent to the serving runtime to cancel the already-scheduled work; the runtime continues and completes the task. If the retried request uses a different idempotency token or no token, the server treats it as a separate invocation.
- Hypothesis B: request-level idempotency is currently applied at request receipt (dedupe for identical token seen within a short window) but tokens supplied by customer are not always propagated to the worker execution metadata (race in header propagation during reconnection). That could allow duplicate executions.
- Reproducer built by Support using Go SDK (attached) shows deterministic duplicate when aborting after 2s and immediately retrying with a different generated request-id.

Immediate workaround suggested to customer:
- Include a stable idempotency key in the retried request (e.g., business-operation-id) that the server will normalize and dedupe on completion.
- As an interim: avoid issuing an immediate retry; wait for the first call timeout or configure a short server-side TTL for in-flight dedupe.

Recommended long-term fixes / follow-ups:
- Server-side: persist idempotency key to funcall execution metadata and perform dedupe on completion, not only on initial receipt. Consider storing key+status (inflight/completed) in the serving control-plane to reject or reconcile retries that occur while execution is inflight.
- SDK: surface a clearer pattern for client cancellation vs intent-to-abort (i.e., provide an explicit "cancel-and-abort-server-work" option) and add docs showing the safe retry pattern for long-running tool calls.

Next steps assigned:
- Engineering (runtime) to validate header propagation path and confirm whether idempotency keys are present on worker-side metadata. (Assigned INT-9923)
- Support to gather a minimal repro that includes headers and request bodies from customer.

Workaround implemented by customer:
- NimbusAI configured their orchestration to attach a stable business id in the metadata and the duplicates dropped to ~0.01% (still visible in narrow edge cases).

Resolution notes (in progress):
- Eng interim patch proposed: ensure idempotency key written to execution record at receipt and atomically used to dedupe completions. Patch PR: runtime#1824 (linked).
